final_answer:
DEVIATION REPORT: Committee redline v. Debtor's Second Amended Plan (Cascadia Timber Holdings, No. 25-30412-MLE, Bankr. D. Or.). For Debtor's counsel before the May 26 position papers and May 28 meet-and-confer. "#" = redline change-log number.

1. BOTTOM LINE
- The redline is not a true comparison to the filed Plan. Its base text differs: classes (redline 1 First Meridian, 2 Timberline, 3 GUC; Plan 1 Priority, 2 First Meridian, 3 Timberline, 4 GUC; Disclosure Statement (DS) Classes 1-7); sections (releases Art. VIII v. Plan Art. X; retention 6.6 v. 5.8; trust 6.7 v. 5.9; MIP 6.4 v. 5.7); text (Plan Supplement 7 days before Voting Deadline v. 14 days before Confirmation Hearing; First Meridian unimpaired v. impaired; Effective Date "first Business Day" after conditions v. 30 days after Final Order); Exhibit A (Ch. 7 GUC 2-5% v. 3-5%), Exhibit B (Year-1 revenue $312M v. $395M) and Exhibit C (7 assumed/5 rejected v. 12/6, different counterparties). Untracked differences exist throughout. Demand a machine comparison against the docketed April 28 Plan (Dkt. 387).
- Of 47 changes, 12 are substantive per the log, and the 16 "semi-substantive" include MIP, board, trustee selection, rejection standard and waiver veto; only 15 are cosmetic. The email's "many are cosmetic" understates.
- Key points: (i) $28.0M at 75/25 creates a roughly $6.5M Effective Date cash shortfall; (ii) 41.07% is supported by Clearview's arithmetic but is an allocation dispute, not clerical; (iii) the Dividend Recap carve-out and supplemental-disclosure condition are the deal-breakers and threaten Timberline's support; (iv) the Debtor's own Plan has exposure (opt-out "non-consensual" releases, Timberline over-recovery, cramdown reliance on an insider-vote class).

2. DEVIATIONS (Plan -> redline; risk)
1) GUC pool (Plan 4.4): $18.7M (10.0%) -> $28.0M (14.97%; $28.0M/$187M). HIGH. Math correct. Email: amount "firm"; comment reserves higher.
2) Timing (#20,21): 50/50 ($9.35M each) -> 75/25 ($21.0M/$7.0M). HIGH. Effective Date uses become $12.5M admin + $3.2M tax + $2.8M priority + $35.0M Timberline + $21.0M = $74.5M v. $68.0M projected cash (DS 9.2): shortfall $6.5M (Debtor's cushion was $5.15M). Clearview s.VI warns acceleration must be tested for §1129(a)(11) feasibility; exit revolver is "TBD." The $3.4M retention bonuses are outside the $62.85M uses; if Administrative Claims (redline 2.1(d)) §1129(a)(9)(A) requires Effective Date cash, shortfall about $9.9M. The redline's own condition 9.1(f) (sufficient cash) would then fail.
3) Interest (#21): none -> §1961 rate on deferred $7.0M, "currently 5.24%" (about $367K; rate unverified; a search suggested about 4.1% in mid-May 2025). Low-cost trade; use actual confirmation-date rate.
4) Avoidance proceeds (Plan 5.9(d): retained by Reorganized Debtor) -> 100% net to GUCs, additive (#9,22,29). HIGH. $9.5M is gross; Clearview excludes it from TEV and flags net/timing uncertainty; Committee's own comment projects net $6.0-7.5M (+3.2-4.0 points), yet redline 20.05% uses gross ($37.5M/$187M). Committee wants both higher pool and all proceeds; trade one against the other.
5) Litigation Trustee (Plan 5.9(b): Reorganized Debtor appoints, Committee consents) -> Committee selects (#28). Accept only with proceeds-sharing resolved; keep $500K funding and three-year term.
6) Equity (Plan 4.3(b), 5.3): Timberline 55% -> 41.07%, remainder 45% -> 58.93% (#6,19,24). Clearview: $60.0M/$146.1M = 41.07% (48.54% low, 35.59% high); 55% implies $80.355M, a $20.355M transfer. But DS 9.1 itself presents 55% x $146.1M = $80.355M as the deal, so "error" is overstated (comment concedes Timberline may disagree). Net of the $35M cash, $60M/$111.1M = 54.0%, an unstated rationale for 55%; disclose methodology. Exposure: $35M + about $80.4M equity = about $115M on a $95M claim (about 121%) while GUCs get 10% invites a fair-and-equitable objection. The redline leaves 58.93% unissued with no recipient. Plan 5.2 lists Timberline's $35M as both payment to Timberline and funding "from Timberline"; DS 6.1 calls it a Timberline contribution; clarify.
7) MIP (Plan 5.7): 10% -> 7% (#11,25). MEDIUM. GUCs get no equity, so the rationale is weak; benefit goes to Timberline/treasury. Answer with comparables.
8) Board (Plan 5.4): 3/1/1 -> Timberline 2, Committee 2, independent 1 (#26). MEDIUM-HIGH. The independent is jointly selected, so Committee plus independent can outvote Timberline despite 41-55% equity; the comment claiming a Timberline majority is wrong. Counter 3/1/1 or 2/2/1 with Timberline-selected independent.
9) Retention $3.4M/12 employees (Plan 5.8; redline 2.1(d), 6.6 struck; #17,27). HIGH. Weaknesses: board-approved Feb. 15, 2025 (16 days pre-petition), recipients include COO/CFO insiders, no §503(c) motion, DS asserts recruiting without bona fide offers. §503(c)(1) bars insider retention payments absent specific findings; whether §503(c) reaches post-confirmation obligations is contestable. File a §503(c) motion with evidence or convert to performance incentives. Email calls it negotiable; comment says strike.
10) New 11.9 (#38,46): Debtor's burden plus "acknowledgment" that bonuses may be junior-held property. Reject (b): bonuses pay for services, not "on account of" junior interests under §1129(b)(2)(B)(ii); do not stipulate. Comment tags it "non-negotiable," beyond the email's three items.
11) Rejection standard (Plan 8.2; redline 7.2): business judgment -> "material net burden" (#30). MEDIUM-HIGH. Departs from §365(a) practice; PacWest ($1.8M/yr) rejection rests on cost savings; threatens $8M savings. Reject; offer objection procedures.
12) Non-consensual releases (Plan 10.4(c); redline 8.2(b) struck, #32). Harrington v. Purdue Pharma L.P., 603 U.S. 204 (2024) bars non-consensual third-party releases; In re Lowenschuss, 67 F.3d 1394 (9th Cir. 1995) is also adverse. Concede, recast as consensual with clear ballot opt-out (sufficiency of opt-out unsettled; D. Or. unverified). Exculpation (Plan 10.3) untouched; check scope under Blixseth v. Credit Suisse, 961 F.3d 1074 (9th Cir. 2020) (unverified).
13) Dividend Recap carve-out (#31,47,33,36). CRITICAL. Excludes Timberline and affiliates from Released Parties, Debtor/Estate release, consensual releases, injunction and discharge for claims "related to" the Sept. 14, 2021 transaction, and transfers them to the Litigation Trust. Email describes only the consensual-release carve-out. Plan 10.4(d) expressly releases these claims and says the Debtor and Committee "reviewed" them; Committee disputes. Merits: DS 3.3 shows Timberline funded the $95M notes, about $88M dividend went to equity holders (Whitaker family about 40%, institutions), with a solvency opinion; the email's claim that Timberline "received distributions" is unsupported by the DS. §548 reaches only transfers within two years of the March 3, 2025 petition, so the email's §548 theory fails on timing; claims must run through §544(b) and Oregon UVTA (ORS 95.200 et seq.; four-year period expiring about Sept. 14, 2025; verify). The same-day Second Lien Notes expose Timberline's $95M claim to §502(d)/§510(c) challenge, a larger lever. Timberline's consent is a "material condition" (Plan 4.3); DS 13.2 flags withdrawal risk.
14) Supplemental disclosure (new 9.1(g); Committee-only waiver; Plan Supplement #34,35,39). CRITICAL. §1125(b) requires adequate information before solicitation, so an Effective Date condition is misplaced; supplement the DS before the June 12 hearing. Item (iv) "Committee's position" should be a Committee-authored insert. The Committee waiver veto is a hold-up right absent from the email. Comment says DS has a "two-sentence mention on page 14"; excerpts show a fuller Section 3.3 (no avoidability analysis). Expect slippage of July 24.
15) Exhibit C (#42-45). Plan already spells "Olympic" correctly (March 15, 2019; $22M/yr; critical to Centralia). Real Plan typos missed: "Febuary" (Northshore), "Cascaede" (Janitorial). #43 (date to 2020) and #45 ($180K to $108K for "Deschutes River Environmental," not on Plan's Exhibit C) are substantive; the email mentions only one misspelling and one date, omitting the dollar change and the PacWest "Industiral" fix. Verify against Claim Nos. 147/203 and Schedules; a wrong date risks misidentifying a $22M contract.
16) Mislabeled cosmetic: Effective Date (#7, "numbering") adds six conditions incl. DIP repayment and sufficient cash; "governmental entity" in Person (#12) widens release/injunction reach; "Reorganized Company" (#1) dual terms; Plan Supplement "list of Exhibits" (#13); voting clarification (#23); new 12.8 reservation of rights (Plan text; move to letter). Accept Ballot, Business Day, time zone, notice emails, Confirmation Date, Administrative Claim/Allowed cross-references.

3. EMAIL v. REDLINE v. SOURCES (red flags)
- Email section cites (5.3(b), 6.4, Art. IX) match neither document set.
- Email's three "non-negotiables" omit 11.9 and the waiver veto, which the redline labels non-negotiable.
- Email: 41.07% "not a point of contention"; comment concedes dispute.
- Clearview errors: weighted midpoint computes to $405.0M, not $407.5M (low $384.3M v. $385M; high $425.8M v. $430M); median of 7.5x/7.8x/8.2x/9.1x is 8.0x, not 7.9x; comparable-company range does not follow from the stated 5-10% discount. At $405.0M, residual equity is $143.6M (41.8%). The report is confidential, Debtor-restricted and FRE 408 designated; determine how the Committee cites its "pp. 8-9."
- Debtor-side inconsistencies the Committee will use: Ch. 7 GUC recovery 3-5% (Plan Ex. A), 0% (DS 11.3), 2-5% (redline); liquidation values $276-334M v. DS $293-349M; 1,200 jobs v. 1,400 employees; Plan Supplement 14 v. 10 days; Year-1 revenue $395M v. Clearview $380M; DS says Timberline takes $35M "in full satisfaction" while Plan adds equity. Fix before June 12.
- Cramdown: DS 13.3 relies on Timberline's class as the accepting impaired class; §1129(a)(10) excludes insiders, and Timberline as sponsor and 2021 lender risks insider status. Secure First Meridian's vote (Plan: impaired; DS: unimpaired).
- Voting leverage: the five Committee members hold $45.2M (24.17% of $187M); §1126(c) acceptance needs two-thirds in amount and over half in number of voting claims, so at full turnout they cannot alone block Class 6 (24.17% is under one-third) but can at lower turnout or with a few more holders. Their stated constituency interests (Northway $14.2M, Deschutes $8.7M, Columbia River $6.1M, Inland Fiber $4.9M, PBGC $11.3M) explain the front-loading ask; Deschutes (lease assumed, cure $210K) and any rejected-contract counterparties benefit personally from the rejection-standard change, a conflict worth noting to the Court. PBGC's priority/pension-termination claim treatment should be confirmed in the GUC pool.
- Time-value check: interest adds only about $0.37M; the real value is the $11.65M accelerated cash, so cash availability, not interest, is the true negotiating variable.
- Effective Date mechanics: redline definition (conditions-based, "first Business Day") replaces the Plan's 30-days-after-Final-Order formulation; conform to avoid inconsistency with Plan 9.2(b) and DS 6.1.
- Source reliability: the Committee email is advocacy; Clearview and the DS are Debtor documents; only the docketed Plan governs (DS 6.2: Plan controls on inconsistency).

4. NEXT STEPS
- By May 22: obtain true comparison; Pinecrest feasibility on $74.5M and $77.9M cases; ask the source of 5.24%.
- May 26 papers. Concede: strike non-consensual release, cosmetic items, real Exhibit C typos, actual-rate interest, Committee role in trustee selection. Counter: pool between $18.7M and $28.0M with lower Effective Date share funded by Timberline or exit revolver; net avoidance sharing in lieu of higher pool; MIP 8-10%; board with Timberline-selected independent; §503(c) motion; reject "material net burden" and 11.9(b).
- Dividend Recap: with Timberline, offer an enhanced DS section before June 12, Rule 2004 access, and tolling or standstill instead of a blanket carve-out; evaluate limitations (§546(a), ORS 95.280) now.
- May 28: state 55% methodology in writing.
- Calendar: June 12 DS hearing; July 24 confirmation; estimated Effective Date Aug. 15, 2025.
Unverified: current §1961 rate; ORS limitation period; Blixseth scope; opt-out sufficiency in D. Or.
